t.7.93.1: Then, after some time had passed, while Rāma remained steadfast on the path of dharma, Kāla, Time itself, came to the royal gate in the guise of an ascetic.
t.7.93.2: He spoke these words to the steadfast and illustrious Lakṣmaṇa: "Announce to Rāma that I have arrived on account of the weight of my business."
t.7.93.4: Having heard those words of his, Saumitri, filled with haste, reported to Rāma what the ascetic wished to say.
t.7.93.3: I am indeed the messenger of an exceedingly mighty great sage of boundless energy. O mighty one, I have come wishing to see Rāma, for I come on a matter of business.
t.7.93.5: Be victorious, O king, through dharma, in both worlds, O greatly radiant one! A messenger has come to see you, an ascetic shining like the sun.
t.7.93.6: Having heard those words spoken by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma said: “Let the sage be brought in, dear one, that greatly powerful bearer of his message.”
t.7.93.7: Saumitri, saying "So be it," led in that sage, who seemed to blaze with splendour and to burn everything with his rays.
t.7.93.8: Approaching the best of the Raghus, who was blazing with his own splendor, the sage said to Rāghava in a sweet voice, "May you prosper!"
t.7.93.10: And when Rāma had asked after his welfare, that most eloquent of speakers, the greatly renowned one, sat down upon a splendid golden seat.
t.7.93.9: The greatly splendid Rāma offered him worship, beginning with the guest-water, and then began to ask after his untroubled welfare.
t.7.93.11: Then Rāma said to him: “Welcome to you, great sage. Deliver the words you bear, since you have come as a messenger.”
t.7.93.12: Urged by the lion among kings, the sage spoke these words: "This must be told between the two of us alone, and my speech must not be spoiled by any other eye."
t.7.93.14: Having promised, "So be it," Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa: "Stand at the door, O mighty-armed one, and dismiss the doorkeeper."
t.7.93.13: Whoever hears or looks upon us, O Rāghava, shall indeed be put to death by you, if you heed the word of the foremost of sages.
t.7.93.15: O Saumitri, whoever should see or hear the conversation spoken between the two of us, the sage and me, he shall surely be put to death by me.
t.7.93.16: Then Kākutstha, having stationed Lakṣmaṇa to guard the door, Rāghava spoke these words to that sage: "Speak."
t.7.93.17: Whatever words you have in mind, or whatever it is on which you are so intent, speak it without misgiving; it dwells in my heart as well.
